Subject: Immediate: us-west-2 AZ1 queue starvation causing 503s (Blue Summit)

Hi Rafael / Marissa / Neha,

We're seeing a severe degradation from our production fleet that started ~08:45 PT. All requests routed to us-west-2:AZ1 (usw2-az1) are showing large queuing delays, token-level latency spikes (p50 380ms -> 2.6s) and a sustained 502/503 error rate ~6% for the last 25 minutes. Throughput has dropped ~40% because clients are retrying — our downstream system (order ingestion) is now queueing at the edge.

We have throttled some traffic at our side to avoid amplifying retries, but the customer impact is material: checkout failures and increased abandonment. They are asking for an immediate cross-region routing option or a manual capacity diversion ASAP.

Attached are a short PCAP and an excerpt of the request/response traces (usw2-az1 error snippets).

Can we stand up an incident bridge and discuss an urgent routing drain to us-east-1 / us-west-1? We need a short-term mitigation and a runbook for next 24 hours.

Sophie Lang
Director, Platform Engineering — Blue Summit Logistics
Sophie.Lang@bluesummit.co

Subject: RE: Immediate: us-west-2 AZ1 queue starvation causing 503s (Blue Summit)

Thanks — joined the bridge and pulled the live metrics. Quick technical read:
- Root cause signal: abrupt KV cache eviction and request-queue buildup on a subset of inference pods in usw2-az1. CPU is fine, but the host-level network receive queue (rx) is spiking and K/V cache misses correlate to the 5xx window.
- We saw increased head-of-line blocking on instances that are running mixed-size sequences — request shaping threshold is being crossed.

Recommended short-term plan (30–90m):
1) Canary steer 15% of traffic away from usw2-az1 -> use1-az2 using control-plane route policy (no DNS TTL change).
2) Increase per-pod concurrency cap on the affected pool (reduce per-request latency variance) and enable temporary prefix-KV cache warming for the hot keyset.
3) If canary shows <1% 5xx and token latency returns to p50 <600ms for 15m, expand to 50% then 100%.
4) If failure persists, failover entire customer route to use1 and schedule a deeper postmortem.

Operational checklist (who/what):
- Rafael: customer comms/exec update; coordinate decision.
- Marissa: approval for routing/credits and CS-directed downstream retries.
- Neha: commercial hedging (credits/SLA messaging).
- Hannah: engineering remediation and monitoring thresholds for rollback.

I'll attach a short trace snippet I captured to the incident Drive (live). Creating JIRA ticket now.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Staff SRE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Blue Summit — approved short-term routing diversion and next steps (BLS-3472)

Team,

Summary:
- Impact: Blue Summit experienced queue starvation in usw2-az1 on 2028-01-17 between 08:45–11:10 PT, producing ~6% 5xx at peak and ~40% throughput degradation.
- Action taken: Controlled canary steer initiated 01/17 11:05 PT at 15% to use1-az2; expanded to 50% at 11:28 PT after 20 minutes of stability; full cutover to use1 completed at 11:46 PT when p50 token latency returned below 500ms.
- Customer-facing outcome: Orders resumed normal ingestion; Blue Summit reported reduced abandonment within 30 minutes of full cutover.

Approved mitigations & follow-ups:
1) Short-term: full routing diversion to use1 (complete).
2) Engineering to perform deep postmortem (root cause: host network rx queue + KV eviction interplay). Target RCA doc by 01/24.
3) Commercial: CS to propose goodwill credit for the degradation window >60 minutes. Neha to own credit proposal.
4) Ops: schedule a focused capacity validation and cold-cache warmup runbook for us-west-2 pools in Q1.

Artifacts: JIRA BLS-3472 (incident ticket), drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/blue-summit/incident-archive, meeting bridge recording: https://meet.google.com/zzz-brid-2028

Action owners:
- Rafael: exec comms + post-incident customer update (by EOD 01/18).
- Marissa: commercial resolution and credit proposal (Neha to collaborate).
- Hannah: remediation patch and RCA doc.
- Neha: commercial credit authorization draft.

If there are objections to the mitigation chosen (full diversion), raise them by EOD 01/18; otherwise I'll proceed with the customer-facing summary and close the bridge.
